messages:
maria: Heads-up — during the canary for 1.2.0-awq-int8 we saw intermittent latency spikes and a handful of 5xxs after increasing AWQ group_size from 64 -> 128. Started at ~1782456900 UTC. RPS unchanged. :eyes:

josh: Any stack traces or logs? Did the runtime log any quantization/activation errors?

maria: No JVM-level OOMs, no container restarts. Attached a snippet from the runtime log around the spike window:

```
2026-03-19T09:15:23.112Z runtime WARN awq: act-quant overflow candidate detected for layer 23, batch 8
2026-03-19T09:15:23.114Z runtime INFO batching: flush triggered, batch_size=12, latency=312ms
2026-03-19T09:15:23.115Z model WARN kv-cache: unexpected kvc miss rate +12%
```

kevin: That `act-quant overflow candidate` message looks suspicious. Could be that increasing group_size changed activation distribution and pushed some ranges outside the expected quant buckets. Did we enable act-quant per-block scaling?

maria: No, this canary used the global act-quant schedule from the bakeoff recipe. We ported the recipe from GPU A to GPU B without re-calibrating.

sophie: On the eval side I started a quick Evals run against the prompt-suite. Quick numbers: baseline FP16 -> AWQ(64) had +0.6% exact-match on our QA set, AWQ(128) is -1.8% relative. MMLU also dropped ~2 points on some subjects. Looks like accuracy drift correlates with the same time window.

metrics-bot: alert: 1782456920 - 1782457100: p50 latency spike 180ms -> 720ms (4x), 5xx rate increased 0.02% -> 0.45% on route /v1/chat/stream-canary

josh: So we have both correctness and latency regressions after group_size bump. Hypothesis: larger group_size increases quantization cross-talk and causes occasional act-levels to saturate causing extra expensive fallback codepaths + KV cache churn.

ciara: Can we repro locally with a narrowed config? I can run the AWQ group sweep on a small synthetic load: group_size [48, 64, 96, 128], act-quant enabled/disabled, activation-clamp thresholds varied.

maria: That would help. Also note the runtime flagged `batch_size=12` in that log; our canary autoscaler sometimes packs more requests into a batch which amplifies act distribution differences.

kevin: If autoscale-batching is amplifying, we should try disabling continuous batching for the canary variant or set max_batch=8 while we debug. Also try group_size=96 — maybe 128 was the breakpoint.

sophie: I pushed a quick eval comparison to the shared sheet: AWQ(96, act-quant on) shows minor delta vs 64 (~-0.2% EM) but AWQ(128, act-quant on) shows larger regressions. With act-quant off both 96 and 128 are worse but flatter.

maria: For immediate mitigation I can pin the canary to AWQ(64) and rollback the group_size change. Prefer hotfix or dynamic rollout?

deploy-bot: deploy: rollback request registered for canary://1.2.0-awq-int8 at 1782457400 by maria — will coordinate with autoscaler guardrails.

ciara: I'll run the local sweep now. Plan: for each group_size run 10k prompt passes at modest concurrency and capture act histograms, kv-miss, p50/p95 latency. I'll post artifacts. ETA ~2h.

josh: Good. Also collect a few raw tensors (quantized/unquantized) for the failing prompts so we can inspect numeric divergence and possibly adjust per-block scale factors.

kevin: Longer term: we should add a quick test to the onboarding pipeline — run AWQ group sensitivity with a 2k prompt sample and ensure no >1% EM drop vs baseline before allowing group_size >96. Keep it lightweight and gated.

maria: Agreed. For now rollback is in progress. We'll follow up with ciara's sweep results and a small postmortem: root cause hypothesis -> group_size boundary + act-quant interaction + batching.

sophie: I'll tag the failing eval seeds in the evals dashboard and create a regression alert so we don't miss this pattern in future model bring-ups.

metrics-bot: info: rollback completed at 1782457600, canary back to AWQ(64) — metrics trending back to baseline.

maria: Thanks everyone. Once ciara posts the sweep artifacts we can decide whether to try a gradual group_score ramp (64 -> 96) with stricter batch caps, or re-tune act-quant per-block. :thumbsup:
